validated_results.title: Associations of specific food sources of dietary fat with prostate cancer incidence and mortality: results from a large prospective cohort.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of 49,424 men reporting a quantitative hazard ratio for intake of fat from dairy and incident prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Quartile 4 vs quartile 1 of fat intake from dairy
extraction.population: Men in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial

sample_size.excerpt: This prospective cohort included 49,424 men from the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial.

cases.excerpt: During follow-up, we documented 4,308 incident cases of PCa, of whom 392 died from PCa.

effect_size.excerpt: When considering available food sources, a greater intake of fat from dairy (HR Q4vs.Q1:1.13; 95% CI: 1.02-1.25; P trend = 0.069) and saturated fatty acids (SFAs) from dairy (HR Q4vs.Q1:1.12; 95% CI: 1.01-1.24; P trend = 0.059) was associated with a higher incidence of PCa in a linear dose-response association (all P non - linearity >0.05).

confidence_interval.excerpt: When considering available food sources, a greater intake of fat from dairy (HR Q4vs.Q1:1.13; 95% CI: 1.02-1.25; P trend = 0.069) and saturated fatty acids (SFAs) from dairy (HR Q4vs.Q1:1.12; 95% CI: 1.01-1.24; P trend = 0.059) was associated with a higher incidence of PCa in a linear dose-response association (all P non - linearity >0.05).

p_value.excerpt: When considering available food sources, a greater intake of fat from dairy (HR Q4vs.Q1:1.13; 95% CI: 1.02-1.25; P trend = 0.069) and saturated fatty acids (SFAs) from dairy (HR Q4vs.Q1:1.12; 95% CI: 1.01-1.24; P trend = 0.059) was associated with a higher incidence of PCa in a linear dose-response association (all P non - linearity >0.05).

validated_results.reason: Original human cross-sectional NHANES analysis reporting an adjusted odds ratio for large caffeine intake and prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Large caffeine intake vs little caffeine consumption
extraction.population: 1789 subjects from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2009 to 2018 waves

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 1789 subjects from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2009 to 2018 waves were enrolled in this study.

effect_size.excerpt: In the fully adjusted model, compared to those reporting little caffeine consumption, those who reported large intake had a multivariate adjusted odd ratio (OR) with 95% confidence interval (CI) of 1.25 (2.21-15.52). Participants with large PA were more likely to develop prostate cancer (OR = 1.68, 95% CI: 1.47-3.80), whereas a significant inverse association between medium PA and prostate cancer was observed (OR = 0.66, 95% CI: 0.48-0.81).
